name: Compressify Image Optimizer – WebP & AVIF
author: Compressify.Net

sections.description:
Compressify Image Optimizer helps you compress WordPress images, convert them to WebP or AVIF, and resize oversized uploads. Optimize new images automatically and process existing images in your media library in the background.

Smaller image files can reduce page weight and image transfer times. Compressify sends images to its external API for processing, so compression and conversion run outside your WordPress hosting environment.

Automatic image compression for new uploads

Enable automatic optimization to compress JPG, PNG, and WebP uploads without manually exporting each file. Choose an output format and adjust image quality to balance file size and appearance.

WebP and AVIF conversion

Convert supported images to WebP or AVIF, or keep a supported original format. Available output formats and usage limits depend on your Compressify plan. AVIF output requires a plan that includes it.

Bulk image optimization for your media library

Process images uploaded before you installed the plugin. Start a background optimization run from the WordPress dashboard and review processing progress and file-size savings.

Resize oversized WordPress images

Set a maximum image width to resize large images during optimization. This can reduce unnecessary image data before it reaches visitors’ browsers.

Image performance and Core Web Vitals

Reducing image size can help pages load faster. When an image is the Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) element, a smaller file can help reduce its download time. Actual results depend on your images, theme, hosting, caching, and other page resources; compression alone does not guarantee a PageSpeed score or Core Web Vitals result.

Connect your Compressify account

A Compressify account and API key are required. A free plan is available with usage limits; paid plans provide additional capacity and features. Check current formats and limits at Compressify.

  1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Open the Compressify settings and connect your account with an API key.
  3. Choose your output format, quality, and optional resize width.
  4. Enable automatic upload optimization or start processing your existing library.

See the External services section below for details about the information sent to Compressify.

External services

This plugin connects to the Compressify API service to optimize images and keep the WordPress site linked with your Compressify workspace.

It sends the following data when you save or rotate the API key and the plugin registers the site with Compressify:
* Site domain
* Site name
* Plugin version
* WordPress version/platform name

It sends the following data during the periodic site heartbeat request:
* Site token
* Plugin version
* WordPress version/platform name

It sends the following data when an upload or background optimization job is processed:
* The image file contents being optimized
* Requested optimization settings such as output format, quality, and resize width when applicable
* Authentication credentials needed to authorize the request

It may also contact the Compressify API to check plugin/API availability for update and status flows.

Service provider: Compressify
Privacy policy: https://compressify.net/privacy
Terms of service: https://compressify.net/terms
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/compressify-net directory, or install the plugin through the WordPress plugins screen directly.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress.
  3. Go to Settings > Compressify in your WordPress dashboard.
  4. Enter your API key from the Compressify dashboard.
  5. Configure your preferred output formats and compression levels.
sections.faq:
Does this require a paid account?

A Compressify account is required. A free plan is available with usage limits. Paid plans offer additional capacity and features; check current plan details at https://compressify.net.

Which image formats are supported?

Compressify supports optimizing JPG, PNG, and WebP files. It can output optimized versions in JPG, PNG, WebP, or AVIF (depending on your plan).

Will it break my existing image links?

The plugin updates attachment files and WordPress attachment metadata during optimization. Format conversion can change file extensions. Back up your media library and test a small batch first, especially if a theme, plugin, or custom code stores direct image URLs outside WordPress attachment metadata.

Can I bulk optimize images already in WordPress?

Yes. Start a background optimization run to process existing media library images. Processing is subject to your account’s usage limits.

Does image compression guarantee better SEO or a perfect PageSpeed score?

No. Smaller images can help reduce page weight and image download times, but search rankings and performance scores depend on many factors. The plugin does not guarantee ranking improvements or specific scores.

Where are images processed?

Images are sent to the external Compressify API for compression, conversion, and optional resizing. See the External services section for the data sent and links to the service’s privacy policy and terms.
